ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Bimodal intensity distribution with a high-intensity (white) to low-intensity (black) pixel ratio of approximately 0.8:1 across the visible fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Solid high-intensity white patches on the distal 40-50% of both lobes; dense black-on-white mottling and stippling at the medial margins of white zones; solid black pigmentation concentrated in the central peduncle area and along the trailing edge center.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Narrow U-shaped notch with an estimated interior angle of 35 degrees; vertical depth occupies approximately 12% of the visible lobe height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular jaggedness along the entire trailing edge; distinct high-amplitude notch/indentation on the left lobe trailing edge near the medial-lateral transition; fine-scale pixel peaks and valleys across distal margins.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex upward curve along the leading edge tapering to acute lateral tips; trailing edge follows a complex multi-inflection path with prominent indentations on the left lobe.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Cluster of 4-5 distinct circular white pixel groups (barnacle scars) located on the medial-ventral region of the right lobe near the transition to the black pigmentation zone.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Faint, roughly parallel vertical linear disruptions (possible rake marks) detected within the white distal pigmentation zone of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Significant irregular tissue loss on the trailing edge of the left lobe; multiple circular depigmented rosette scars concentrated on the inner right lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: Asymmetric mottling density; the right lobe contains a higher frequency of small black focal spots within the distal white region compared to the more solid white region of the left lobe.
